column3: The Hebrew asks about gazing at a virgin without separately naming desire; BSB explicitly adds desire.
The Hebrew first names a woman without identifying her as the neighbor’s wife; BSB identifies her before mentioning his door.
The Hebrew says others should bow down over her; BSB explicitly describes sleeping with her.
The Hebrew says God rises and visits without separately naming judgment or being called to account; BSB supplies those descriptions.
The Hebrew first says him in the singular; BSB says them.
The Hebrew makes his loins bless the speaker; BSB names his heart.
The Hebrew names a shoulder falling and an arm being broken; BSB makes an arm fall and be torn from its socket.
The Hebrew names light; BSB identifies it as the sun.
The Hebrew makes his hand kiss his mouth; BSB describes throwing a kiss from his mouth.
The Hebrew names his palate; BSB says his mouth.
